introduction: Today we begin Holy Week. We welcome Jesus into Jerusalem with palm branches, as the crowds cry, Hosanna to the Son of David. Then we hear the account of his Passion according to Saint Matthew. The servant in Isaiah does not turn back from insult; Paul sings of Christ who humbled himself unto death on a cross. Let us walk with Jesus this week, from the palms to the cross and the empty tomb.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ humbled himself and became obedient to death. Let us pray to the Father, who exalted him.
intentions: For the Church as she enters Holy Week: that she may follow her Lord with faith and love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace in Jerusalem and in every land torn by violence: that the King who comes humbly may bring peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are betrayed, abandoned or condemned unjustly: that they may find strength in the suffering Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who, like Peter, have denied the Lord: that they may weep and return to him. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may watch and pray with Jesus this week. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty Father, your Son entered Jerusalem to give his life for us. Help us to follow him faithfully this week, and to share in his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Truly this was the Son of God
reflection.body:
Holy Week opens with a procession. Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey, fulfilling the prophecy: "behold, your King comes to you, humble, and riding on a donkey." The crowds spread their cloaks and branches on the road and shout, "Hosanna to the son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!" The whole city asks, "Who is this?"

Then, at the same Mass, we hear Matthew's account of the Passion. Judas sells his master for thirty pieces of silver. At the Last Supper, Jesus gives his disciples his Body and Blood: "this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins."

In Gethsemane, Jesus is "sorrowful and severely troubled." He prays, "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire." His disciples fall asleep, and he asks Peter, "What, couldn't you watch with me for one hour?"

Judas betrays him with a kiss. When one of the disciples draws a sword, Jesus says, "Put your sword back into its place, for all those who take the sword will die by the sword." Peter denies him three times, and when the rooster crows, "he went out and wept bitterly." Judas, filled with remorse, says, "I have sinned in that I betrayed innocent blood."

On the cross, Jesus is mocked: "He saved others, but he can't save himself." He cries out the opening words of Psalm 22: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" When he dies, the earth shakes, and the centurion says, "Truly this was the Son of God!"

This week, keep watch with Jesus. Take part in the liturgies of the Triduum if you can. And place your palm near a crucifix at home, as a reminder to stay with him.
